question.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}, & 0\le x<1 \\ \frac{1}{2}\,x, & 1\le x\le 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{4}].$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the fourth raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{4}] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{4}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{4}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{4}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{20}\,{x}^{5}\,{|}_{0}^{1}+\frac{1}{12}\,{x}^{6}\,{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{20}(1-0)+\frac{1}{12}(64-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{20}+\frac{21}{4} \\  & =\frac{53}{10}\end{aligned}
$$
